questions.explanation: Abiotic factors are non-living physical and chemical conditions. The others are biotic, caused by living organisms.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: Which of these is a biotic factor affecting the distribution of organisms?
questions.explanation: Biotic factors come from interactions between living organisms.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: The relative humidity of the air in a habitat is measured with a
questions.explanation: The difference between the wet-bulb and dry-bulb readings gives the relative humidity.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: A rain gauge is used to measure
questions.explanation: Rain is collected in a funnel and measured in millimetres.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: In studying a pond, a Secchi disc is used to measure
options: how far light penetrates the water (its turbidity)
questions.explanation: The depth at which the black and white disc disappears from view shows how clear the water is.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: Wind speed in a habitat is measured with
questions.explanation: Wind affects transpiration and the dispersal of seeds and spores.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: Few green plants grow on the floor of a dense tropical rainforest mainly because
options: the soil there has no water
the thick canopy lets very little light reach the ground
the temperature there is too low
questions.explanation: Light is the limiting factor, so only shade-tolerant plants survive on the forest floor.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: Which of these is an edaphic (soil) factor?
questions.explanation: Edaphic factors include soil texture, pH, water and mineral content.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: Salinity (salt content of water) is a major factor controlling which organisms live in
questions.explanation: Organisms there must cope with water whose salt content changes with the tides.

questions.topic: Factors affecting the distribution of organisms
questions.stem: A quadrat is used in ecological studies mainly to
options: estimate the abundance or density of plants and slow-moving animals in an area
questions.explanation: Organisms are counted in squares of known area that are placed at random, and the results are scaled up for the whole area.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: In a food chain, green plants are described as
questions.explanation: Green plants trap light energy and make food, which starts the food chain.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: In the food chain grass -> grasshopper -> lizard -> hawk, the lizard is the
questions.explanation: The lizard eats the primary consumer (the grasshopper), so it is at the third trophic level.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Energy decreases along a food chain mainly because at each trophic level much of it is
questions.explanation: Only about 10% of the energy at one level is passed on to the next.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Producers in an ecosystem store 50 000 kJ of energy. If about 10% of the energy is passed on at each trophic level, how much energy reaches the tertiary consumers?
questions.explanation: Primary consumers get 5000 kJ, secondary consumers 500 kJ and tertiary consumers 50 kJ.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: A pyramid of numbers is inverted (narrow at the base) when
options: a field of grass supports a few cows
a single large tree supports many caterpillars
many insects support a few birds
questions.explanation: One producer can feed many herbivores, so the base of the pyramid is the smallest bar.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi are important in an ecosystem because they
options: break down dead organisms and return mineral nutrients to the soil
questions.explanation: Without decomposers, nutrients would stay locked in dead bodies.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: A lichen is an association between
options: an alga and a fungus, in which both partners benefit
questions.explanation: The alga photosynthesises and the fungus gives water, minerals and protection. This is mutualism.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: The nitrogen-fixing bacteria found in the root nodules of leguminous plants belong to the genus
questions.explanation: Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen into compounds the plant can use, and receives sugars in return.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Denitrifying bacteria in waterlogged soils
questions.explanation: Denitrification lowers soil fertility. It is common where oxygen is scarce.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: In the nitrogen cycle, Nitrosomonas bacteria convert
questions.explanation: This is the first step of nitrification. Nitrobacter then converts nitrites into nitrates.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Nitrobacter bacteria in the soil
questions.explanation: Nitrates are the main form of nitrogen that plant roots absorb.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Lightning contributes to the nitrogen cycle by
options: combining nitrogen and oxygen into oxides of nitrogen, which reach the soil as nitrates in rain
questions.explanation: The high energy of lightning makes N2 react with O2.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Which process removes carbon(IV) oxide from the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Green plants fix CO2 into sugars. The other processes release CO2.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Which human activity adds carbon(IV) oxide to the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Combustion releases carbon that was stored in coal, oil and gas for millions of years.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: In the water cycle, water vapour is released into the atmosphere from leaves by
questions.explanation: Transpiration and evaporation return water vapour to the air.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: The relationship in which one organism benefits and the other is neither harmed nor helped is
questions.explanation: An example is an epiphytic orchid growing on a tree branch, which gets a position in the light without harming the tree.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: A tick feeding on the blood of a cow is an example of
questions.explanation: The tick benefits and the cow is harmed.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: A food web is
options: a single straight line of feeding relationships
the web built by a spider
a network of interconnected food chains in a community
questions.explanation: Most animals eat more than one kind of food, so food chains link up to form webs.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: In a grassland food web, hawks feed on both snakes and rats, and snakes also eat rats. If the hawks were removed, the most likely immediate effect would be
options: an increase in the numbers of snakes and rats
a decrease in the numbers of snakes
an increase in the amount of grass
questions.explanation: With no hawks hunting them, more snakes and rats survive. More rats would then eat more grass.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: Primary consumers in a food chain are
questions.explanation: They feed directly on the producers (plants).

questions.stem: Mangrove swamps in Nigeria are found mainly
options: along the coast and in estuaries, where the water is brackish
questions.explanation: Mangroves are common in the Niger Delta and the Lagos lagoon.

questions.stem: Many mangrove trees have pneumatophores (breathing roots) because
options: the waterlogged mud they grow in has very little oxygen
questions.explanation: These roots grow upwards above the mud and take in air through pores.

questions.stem: Plankton are
options: organisms that live in the soil
tiny organisms that drift in water
questions.explanation: Phytoplankton are producers and zooplankton are consumers. Together they form the base of aquatic food chains.

questions.stem: Animals that live in fast-flowing streams are often adapted by having
options: suckers or hooks for clinging to stones, and flattened or streamlined bodies
questions.explanation: These features stop them being washed away by the current.

questions.stem: The prehensile (grasping) tail of some monkeys is an adaptation for life
questions.explanation: The tail acts as an extra limb for holding branches.

questions.stem: Burrowing mammals usually have
options: strong claws and powerful forelimbs for digging
questions.explanation: These help them dig tunnels for shelter and safety.

questions.stem: Barnacles and limpets survive strong wave action on rocky seashores because they
questions.explanation: Their shells and firm grip also stop them drying out at low tide.

questions.stem: Floating water plants such as water lettuce (Pistia) stay afloat mainly because they
options: have deep roots fixed in the mud
have air spaces (aerenchyma) in their tissues
questions.explanation: Air-filled tissues make them buoyant and also supply oxygen to submerged parts.

questions.stem: In Nigeria, tropical rainforest is found mainly in the
questions.explanation: High rainfall and humidity in the south support dense forest.

questions.stem: Which set of features describes the tropical rainforest?
options: Low rainfall, short grasses and very few trees
Heavy rainfall, tall evergreen trees in several layers, many climbers and epiphytes
questions.explanation: Rainforest vegetation is layered (stratified) and very rich in species.

questions.stem: The Sudan savanna of northern Nigeria is characterised by
options: short grasses with scattered, short trees and a long dry season
tall grasses up to 3 metres with gallery forests
questions.explanation: Rainfall is lower and the dry season longer than in the Guinea savanna.

questions.stem: The Guinea savanna, which lies between the rainforest and the Sudan savanna, is characterised by
options: tall grasses and scattered trees, many with thick, fire-resistant bark
questions.explanation: Bush fires are common in the dry season, so many trees are protected by thick bark.

questions.stem: Montane forests and grasslands are found in Nigeria on the
questions.explanation: High altitude gives cooler temperatures, which favour montane vegetation.

questions.stem: Desert plants are adapted to survive by having
options: very deep or widespread roots and small or spiny leaves
large, thin leaves with many stomata
questions.explanation: These features help them to get water and to reduce water loss.

questions.stem: Many trees in the savanna shed their leaves during the dry season in order to
questions.explanation: With little water in the soil, losing leaves stops water being lost through them.

questions.stem: Lianas (woody climbers) are especially common in the
questions.explanation: They climb up the trees to reach light at the canopy.

questions.stem: Travelling from the coast at the Niger Delta northwards to the far north of Nigeria, the main vegetation zones occur in which order?
options: Sahel savanna -> Sudan savanna -> Guinea savanna -> rainforest -> mangrove swamp
Rainforest -> mangrove swamp -> Sudan savanna -> Guinea savanna -> Sahel savanna
Mangrove swamp -> rainforest -> Guinea savanna -> Sudan savanna -> Sahel savanna
Mangrove swamp -> Guinea savanna -> rainforest -> Sahel savanna -> Sudan savanna
questions.explanation: Rainfall decreases from south to north, so the vegetation changes from swamp and forest to drier and drier grassland.

questions.stem: The Sahel savanna in the far north of Nigeria has
options: the lowest rainfall of the Nigerian biomes, with sparse grasses and thorny shrubs
questions.explanation: It borders the Sahara desert and has a very long dry season.

questions.stem: A population is best defined as
options: all the organisms of different species in an area
the non-living parts of an ecosystem
the total number of habitats in a region
all the organisms of one species living in a particular area
questions.explanation: A community is made up of the populations of all the species in an area.

questions.stem: A rectangular plot measuring 4 m by 5 m contains 240 plants of a weed species. What is the population density of the weed?
questions.explanation: Area = 4 x 5 = 20 m^2, and density = 240/20 = 12 plants per m^2.

questions.stem: In a capture-recapture study, 60 snails were marked and released. Later, 50 snails were caught, of which 10 were marked. What is the estimated size of the snail population?
questions.explanation: Population = (number first marked x total in second catch) / number recaptured = (60 x 50)/10 = 300.

questions.stem: Intraspecific competition is competition between
questions.explanation: Members of the same species need exactly the same resources, so this competition is usually intense.

questions.stem: Interspecific competition takes place when
options: members of the same species compete for mates
two organisms live together and both benefit
two different species compete for the same limited resource
questions.explanation: For example, two kinds of grass may compete for light and nutrients.

questions.stem: Overcrowding in a population usually leads to
options: more competition for food and space and faster spread of disease
questions.explanation: High density increases stress on resources and makes it easier for disease to spread.

questions.stem: Primary succession begins on
options: bare rock or new land where there is no soil
questions.explanation: Pioneer organisms must first help to form soil.

questions.stem: Which organisms are usually the first to colonise bare rock?
questions.explanation: Lichens can survive with no soil. They weather the rock and add organic matter.

questions.stem: The final, stable community at the end of an ecological succession is called the
questions.explanation: It stays more or less unchanged unless it is disturbed, for example by fire or farming.

questions.stem: Weeds, then shrubs and finally trees growing on abandoned farmland is an example of
questions.explanation: The soil is already there, so secondary succession is faster than primary succession.

questions.stem: A population of yeast cells grown in a fixed amount of nutrient shows an S-shaped (sigmoid) growth curve. The phases of this curve, in order, are
options: exponential phase, lag phase, stationary phase
stationary phase, lag phase, exponential phase
lag phase, exponential (log) phase, stationary phase
death phase, lag phase, exponential phase
questions.explanation: Growth is slow at first, then rapid, and then levels off as resources run out.

questions.stem: Which of these is a density-dependent factor that limits population size?
questions.explanation: Disease spreads more easily in crowded populations. Natural disasters affect populations whatever their density.

questions.stem: In population studies, natality refers to the
options: movement of individuals into an area
movement of individuals out of an area
questions.explanation: Mortality is the death rate. Immigration is movement in and emigration is movement out.

questions.stem: A population of 2000 rabbits had 100 births and 40 deaths in one year. During the same year, 30 rabbits moved in and 10 moved out. What was the population at the end of the year?
A plant species was found in 12 out of 40 quadrats placed at random in a field. What is its percentage frequency?
Sandy soil drains quickly because
options: its large particles leave large air spaces between them
it contains a lot of humus
questions.explanation: Large pores let water pass through easily, so sandy soil holds little water and minerals are washed out.

questions.stem: Clay soil tends to become waterlogged because
options: its very fine particles leave tiny pores, so water drains slowly
it contains no water at all
questions.explanation: Clay holds a lot of water but is poorly aerated and sticky when wet.

questions.stem: Loamy soil is the best soil for most crops because it
options: has a balanced mixture of sand, silt, clay and humus, so it drains well but holds enough water
questions.explanation: Loam combines good drainage, good water retention, good aeration and fertility.

questions.stem: Water rises highest by capillarity in a column of
questions.explanation: The fine pores between clay particles act like very narrow tubes.

questions.stem: Equal masses of dry sand, loam and clay were placed in funnels, and 100 cm^3 of water was poured onto each. The volume of water that drained through was measured. Which result is expected?
options: The least water drained through the sand
Equal volumes drained through all three soils
The most water drained through the clay
The least water drained through the clay, because clay retains the most water
questions.explanation: Sand retains the least water and clay the most. Loam lies in between.

questions.stem: Humus improves the soil because it
options: makes the soil more acidic and sterile
holds water, supplies nutrients and improves soil structure
questions.explanation: Humus is decomposed organic matter that binds soil particles into crumbs.

questions.stem: To find the volume of air in a soil sample, a known volume of soil is added to a known volume of water. The total volume afterwards is less than the sum of the two volumes. The difference represents the
options: volume of water in the soil
volume of humus in the soil
volume of air that was in the soil
questions.explanation: Water fills the air spaces and drives the air out, so the combined volume goes down.

questions.stem: Which of these practices leads to loss of soil fertility?
options: Planting the same crop on the same land year after year
questions.explanation: Continuous cropping removes the same nutrients repeatedly. Leaching and erosion also reduce fertility.

questions.stem: Including legumes such as cowpea in a crop rotation helps to maintain soil fertility because
options: they remove all the nitrogen from the soil
they prevent the growth of soil bacteria
their root nodules contain bacteria that fix nitrogen
questions.explanation: Nitrogen-fixing Rhizobium adds nitrogen compounds to the soil.

questions.stem: Earthworms improve soil fertility by
options: burrowing, which aerates and drains the soil, and by mixing organic matter into it
questions.explanation: Their casts also bring finer soil to the surface.

questions.stem: The water held as a thin film around soil particles, which plants can absorb, is called
questions.explanation: Gravitational water drains away quickly, and hygroscopic water is held too tightly for roots to take up.

questions.stem: Bush burning during land clearing reduces soil fertility in the long term because it
options: destroys humus and kills useful soil organisms
questions.explanation: Ash gives a short-term supply of minerals, but organic matter and soil life are lost.

questions.stem: Cholera is caused by
options: a fungus spread through the air
a protozoan spread by tsetse flies
a bacterium spread mainly through water and food contaminated with faeces
questions.explanation: Vibrio cholerae causes severe diarrhoea. Clean water and good sanitation prevent its spread.

questions.stem: Tuberculosis is caused by
options: a bacterium, and is spread by droplets coughed into the air
a virus spread by sexual contact
questions.explanation: Mycobacterium tuberculosis mainly attacks the lungs. The BCG vaccine gives protection.

questions.stem: Poliomyelitis is
options: a bacterial disease cured by antibiotics
a fungal infection of the skin
a viral disease that can cause paralysis and is prevented by vaccination
a disease caused by lack of vitamin D
questions.explanation: Oral polio vaccine campaigns have greatly reduced cases in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Gonorrhoea is a sexually transmitted infection caused by
questions.explanation: Neisseria gonorrhoeae can be treated with antibiotics.

questions.stem: Syphilis is caused by
questions.explanation: If untreated, syphilis can damage the heart and nervous system.

questions.stem: HIV causes AIDS by attacking
options: a type of white blood cell (helper T-lymphocytes), which weakens the immune system
questions.explanation: With a weakened immune system, opportunistic infections take hold.

questions.stem: HIV is NOT transmitted by
questions.explanation: The virus is passed on through blood and sexual fluids, not by casual contact.

questions.stem: River blindness (onchocerciasis) is transmitted by the
questions.explanation: Blackflies breed in fast-flowing rivers, which is how the disease got its name.

questions.stem: Sleeping sickness (trypanosomiasis) is transmitted by the
questions.explanation: The tsetse fly carries Trypanosoma, a protozoan parasite.

questions.stem: People become infected with guinea worm by
options: drinking unfiltered water containing tiny crustaceans (Cyclops) that carry the larvae
questions.explanation: Filtering or boiling drinking water breaks the cycle.

questions.stem: The intermediate host of the parasite that causes schistosomiasis (bilharzia) is
questions.explanation: Larvae released from snails penetrate the skin of people who wade or swim in infected water.

questions.stem: Which measure helps to prevent malaria?
questions.explanation: Nets stop the female Anopheles mosquito from biting at night.

questions.stem: In a sewage treatment plant, the sewage is aerated (supplied with air) in order to
options: help aerobic bacteria break down organic matter
questions.explanation: Aerobic decomposers oxidise the organic waste to harmless products.

questions.stem: When fertilisers are washed from farms into a lake, the water may become green with algae and later fish may die. This process is called
questions.explanation: The algae and plants that grow on the extra nutrients die, and bacteria decomposing them use up the dissolved oxygen.

questions.stem: The main purpose of game reserves and national parks is to
options: protect wildlife and their habitats from destruction and extinction
questions.explanation: They conserve biodiversity and also support tourism and research.

questions.stem: Which of these is a national park in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Kainji Lake National Park, in Niger and Kwara States, protects savanna wildlife. The others are natural landmarks.

questions.stem: Forests are described as a renewable natural resource because
options: they can be replaced by replanting, if they are managed well
questions.explanation: Trees grow back. Fossil fuels and minerals are non-renewable.

questions.stem: Large-scale deforestation can lead to
options: soil erosion and loss of wildlife habitats
a decrease in atmospheric carbon(IV) oxide
questions.explanation: Without tree cover, soil is exposed to rain and wind, and animals lose their homes.

questions.stem: Vaccination protects against a disease by
options: killing all bacteria in the body
curing the disease after it has developed
stimulating the body to produce antibodies and memory cells against the disease-causing organism
questions.explanation: A weakened or dead form of the pathogen, or part of it, prepares the immune system to respond quickly to a real infection.

questions.stem: Ringworm, a skin infection that forms circular patches, is caused by
questions.explanation: Despite its name, ringworm is a fungal infection. It is spread by contact.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of continuous variation in humans?
questions.explanation: Height shows a range of values with no clear-cut groups. The others are either-or traits.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of discontinuous variation?
questions.explanation: Each person belongs to one distinct group (A, B, AB or O), with no in-between values.

questions.stem: Fingerprints are used in crime detection because
options: each person's fingerprint pattern is unique and does not change during life
all members of a family have identical fingerprints
fingerprints show a person's blood group
questions.explanation: Even identical twins have different fingerprints.

questions.stem: Whether or not a person can roll their tongue is an example of
options: discontinuous variation that is controlled by genes
continuous variation caused by the environment
questions.explanation: A person either can or cannot roll the tongue.

questions.stem: Some people find the chemical phenylthiocarbamide (PTC) very bitter, while others cannot taste it. This is an example of
questions.explanation: It is a difference in body function (taste perception), and it is inherited.

questions.stem: A person with blood group O is often called a universal donor because their red blood cells
options: carry both A and B antigens
carry neither A nor B antigens
questions.explanation: With no A or B antigens, the donated cells are not clumped by the recipient's antibodies.

questions.stem: A person with blood group AB is called a universal recipient because their plasma
options: contains both anti-A and anti-B antibodies
contains neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies
questions.explanation: Their plasma will not clump any donated red cells of the ABO system.

questions.stem: From which blood groups can a person of blood group A safely receive blood?
questions.explanation: Group A plasma contains anti-B antibodies, so it would clump B and AB red cells.

questions.stem: A child has blood group O and the mother has blood group A. Which of these men could NOT be the child's father?
options: A man of blood group O
A man of blood group A
A man of blood group AB
A man of blood group B
questions.explanation: A child of group O must receive an O allele from each parent. A man of group AB (genotype AB) has no O allele to pass on.

questions.stem: Which of these is a cause of genetic variation among offspring?
options: Crossing over and independent assortment during meiosis
questions.explanation: Meiosis and random fertilisation shuffle the alleles. Diet and exercise cause non-heritable (environmental) variation.

questions.stem: A histogram of the heights of pupils in a large school usually shows
options: two separate peaks with nothing between them
all pupils of exactly the same height
questions.explanation: Continuous variation produces a smooth, bell-shaped spread around the average.

questions.stem: Identical twins raised in different homes grow up with noticeably different body masses. This difference is mainly due to
options: environmental factors such as diet and exercise
questions.explanation: Identical twins have the same genes, so differences between them are environmental.

questions.stem: During a blood transfusion, agglutination (clumping) occurs when
options: donor and recipient have the same blood group
the blood is stored in a refrigerator
the donor has blood group O
the antibodies in the recipient's plasma react with the antigens on the donor's red cells
questions.explanation: Clumped cells can block blood vessels, which may be fatal.

questions.stem: The plasma of a person with blood group A contains
options: no antibodies of the ABO system
questions.explanation: People do not make antibodies against their own antigens.

questions.stem: A gene is best described as
options: a unit of inheritance found on a chromosome
questions.explanation: Genes are sections of DNA that control particular characteristics.

questions.stem: Mendel's first law, the law of segregation, states that
options: the two alleles of a gene separate during gamete formation, so each gamete gets only one
characteristics acquired during life are inherited
questions.explanation: Each gamete carries one allele of each gene, and fertilisation brings two together again.

questions.stem: Alleles are
options: different forms of the same gene
questions.explanation: For example, T (tall) and t (short) are alleles of the gene for height in pea plants.

questions.stem: An organism with two identical alleles for a characteristic (for example TT or tt) is described as
questions.explanation: A heterozygous organism has two different alleles, such as Tt.

questions.stem: The phenotype of an organism is
options: its observable characteristics, which result from its genotype and environment
questions.explanation: Genotype means the alleles present. Phenotype means what is actually seen.

questions.stem: In pea plants, tall (T) is dominant to short (t). What phenotypic ratio is expected when two heterozygous tall plants (Tt) are crossed?
questions.explanation: Tt x Tt gives 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so 3 are tall for every 1 short.

questions.stem: A heterozygous tall pea plant (Tt) is crossed with a short plant (tt). What ratio of offspring is expected?
questions.explanation: Tt x tt gives 1 Tt : 1 tt.

questions.stem: What fraction of the offspring of a cross between two heterozygous parents (Aa x Aa) is expected to be homozygous recessive?
questions.explanation: The offspring are 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa, so 1 in 4 is aa.

questions.stem: In cattle, black coat (B) is dominant to red coat (b). A black bull mated with several red cows produced both black and red calves. What is the genotype of the bull?
options: It cannot be worked out from this information
questions.explanation: Red calves (bb) must have received a b allele from the bull, so the black bull must be Bb.

questions.stem: A test cross is used to find out whether an organism showing the dominant characteristic is homozygous or heterozygous. It is done by crossing the organism with
questions.explanation: If any offspring show the recessive characteristic, the organism being tested must be heterozygous.

questions.stem: In humans, the sex of a baby is determined by the father because
options: his sperm all carry Y chromosomes
the mother produces both X and Y eggs
his sperm carry either an X or a Y chromosome, while all eggs carry an X
questions.explanation: An X sperm gives a girl (XX) and a Y sperm gives a boy (XY).

questions.stem: What is the probability that any one child born to a couple will be a boy?
questions.explanation: Half of the sperm carry a Y chromosome, so each birth has an equal chance of being a boy or a girl.

questions.stem: A couple already has three daughters. What is the probability that their next child will be a boy?
questions.explanation: Each birth is an independent event, so earlier births do not change the chance, which stays 1/2.

questions.stem: Haemophilia is much more common in males than in females because
options: it is carried on the Y chromosome
the recessive allele is carried on the X chromosome and males have only one X chromosome
females cannot inherit it at all
questions.explanation: A single recessive allele on a male's X chromosome is expressed, because there is no second X to mask it.

questions.stem: A woman who is a carrier of haemophilia (XHXh) marries a man with normal blood clotting (XHY). What proportion of their sons would be expected to have haemophilia?
questions.explanation: Sons receive their X chromosome from their mother. Half of her eggs carry Xh, so half the sons are expected to be XhY (haemophiliac).

questions.stem: A colour-blind man (XcY) marries a woman who is homozygous for normal vision (XCXC). What are their daughters expected to be?
questions.explanation: Every daughter gets Xc from her father and XC from her mother, so she is XCXc: she has normal vision but is a carrier.

questions.stem: A normal human gamete contains
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the diploid number (46), so the gametes are haploid.

questions.stem: In a DNA molecule, adenine always pairs with
questions.explanation: A pairs with T and G pairs with C. Uracil is found in RNA, not DNA.

questions.stem: People with the haemoglobin genotype AS (sickle-cell trait)
options: are usually healthy carriers and have some resistance to malaria
cannot pass on the S allele
questions.explanation: They have both normal and sickle haemoglobin, so they rarely show symptoms.

questions.stem: Two people who both have the genotype AS plan to marry. What is the probability that any one of their children will have the genotype SS?
questions.explanation: AS x AS gives 1 AA : 2 AS : 1 SS. This is why genotype testing before marriage is advised.

questions.stem: Red-flowered plants crossed with white-flowered plants of the same species give pink-flowered offspring. Pink is the result of
questions.explanation: Neither allele fully masks the other. Crossing two pink plants gives red : pink : white in the ratio 1 : 2 : 1.

questions.stem: Meiosis differs from mitosis in that meiosis
options: produces four haploid cells that are genetically different
involves no division of the nucleus
questions.explanation: Meiosis makes gametes. Mitosis is for growth and repair.

questions.stem: Crossing over between homologous chromosomes takes place during
questions.explanation: Pairs of chromosomes exchange segments in the first prophase of meiosis, which produces new combinations of alleles.

questions.stem: An important application of genetics in agriculture is
options: breeding crops and livestock that give high yields and resist disease
questions.explanation: Selective breeding combines desirable traits, as in improved varieties of maize and cassava.

questions.stem: Genetic counselling helps intending couples mainly by
options: choosing the sex of their children
advising them of the risk of passing on inherited disorders such as sickle-cell anaemia
questions.explanation: Knowing their genotypes helps couples make informed decisions.

questions.stem: A sudden, heritable change in the genetic material of an organism is called
questions.explanation: Mutations can be caused by radiation or chemicals, or can happen by chance.

questions.stem: Down's syndrome is caused by
questions.explanation: Affected people have 47 chromosomes instead of 46.

questions.stem: A person whose ABO blood group genotype is I^A I^O has blood group
questions.explanation: I^A is dominant to I^O, so the A antigen is produced.

questions.stem: A man with genotype I^A I^B marries a woman with genotype I^O I^O. Which blood groups are possible among their children?
questions.explanation: The children receive I^A or I^B from the father and I^O from the mother, so they are I^A I^O (group A) or I^B I^O (group B).

questions.stem: Lamarck's theory of evolution is based on
options: use and disuse of organs and the inheritance of acquired characteristics
natural selection and survival of the fittest
questions.explanation: Lamarck believed that changes an organism acquired during its life were passed on to its offspring.

questions.stem: Darwin's theory of evolution is based mainly on
questions.explanation: Individuals with useful variations survive and reproduce more, and they pass these variations on.

questions.stem: According to Lamarck, giraffes developed long necks because
options: giraffes with naturally longer necks survived better and had more young
mutations happened in response to the need for longer necks
their ancestors stretched their necks to reach leaves, and the longer necks were passed on to their offspring
questions.explanation: This is Lamarck's idea of use and inheritance. The second explanation is Darwin's.

questions.stem: A major objection to Lamarck's theory is that
options: characteristics acquired during an organism's life, such as large muscles from weightlifting, are not passed on to offspring
all organisms produce the same number of offspring
questions.explanation: Changes to body cells do not alter the genes in the gametes.

questions.stem: Darwin noted that finches on the Galapagos Islands had beaks of different shapes. He explained this as
options: adaptation to different food sources through natural selection
the result of the birds using their beaks more
beaks changing during each bird's lifetime
mutation caused by the birds' needs
questions.explanation: Each beak shape suited the food available on that island.

questions.stem: Organic evolution can be defined as
options: the growth of an individual from birth to death
the gradual change in living organisms over many generations, giving rise to new species
the sudden appearance of complex organisms
questions.explanation: Evolution happens to populations over long periods of time.

questions.stem: In industrial areas of Britain, dark forms of the peppered moth became more common than pale forms when tree trunks were blackened by soot. This is best explained by
options: the moths becoming darker by absorbing soot
Lamarck's theory of use and disuse
natural selection, because birds found and ate more of the pale moths on dark trunks
all the pale moths migrating away
questions.explanation: The dark moths were better camouflaged, so more of them survived to reproduce.

questions.stem: One of Darwin's observations was that organisms produce far more offspring than can survive. This leads to
questions.explanation: Limited resources mean that only some individuals survive to reproduce.

questions.stem: Fossils provide evidence for evolution because they
options: show that all organisms appeared at the same time
show the remains of organisms that lived in the past and how they changed over time
questions.explanation: Fossils in successive rock layers show a sequence of changing forms.

questions.stem: The forelimb of a human, the wing of a bat and the flipper of a whale have the same basic bone structure but different functions. They are examples of
questions.explanation: The shared pentadactyl pattern suggests that these animals had a common ancestor.

questions.stem: The wings of a bird and the wings of a butterfly are
options: homologous structures with the same origin
evidence that birds evolved from insects
analogous structures, which have the same function but different origins
questions.explanation: Analogous structures arise when unrelated organisms adapt to similar ways of life.

questions.stem: Which of these is a vestigial organ in humans?
questions.explanation: Vestigial organs are reduced remnants of organs that were functional in ancestors.

questions.stem: Early embryos of fish, birds and mammals look alike and all have gill pouches. This suggests that
options: all vertebrates breathe with gills as adults
questions.explanation: This is the evidence from comparative embryology.

questions.stem: Similarities in the DNA and protein sequences of different species provide evidence of evolution because
options: closely related species have more similar sequences
DNA does not change over time
proteins are found only in animals
questions.explanation: The fewer the differences between two species, the more recently they shared a common ancestor.

questions.stem: Pouched mammals (marsupials) such as kangaroos are found naturally mainly in Australia. This is an example of evidence of evolution from
questions.explanation: Australia was isolated early, so marsupials evolved there without competition from placental mammals.

questions.stem: The development of resistance to antibiotics in bacteria is an example of
options: evolution by natural selection happening today
questions.explanation: Resistant bacteria survive treatment and multiply, so resistance spreads through the population.

questions.stem: In undisturbed layers of sedimentary rock, the deepest (oldest) layers usually contain fossils of
options: more complex organisms than the upper layers
simpler organisms than the upper (younger) layers
questions.explanation: The fossil record shows that life became more complex over time.

questions.stem: In a plant, tall (T) is dominant to short (t), and red flowers (R) are dominant to white flowers (r). The two genes are on different chromosomes. What fraction of the offspring of the cross TtRr x TtRr is expected to be tall with red flowers?
questions.explanation: A dihybrid cross of two double heterozygotes gives the ratio 9 : 3 : 3 : 1. The 9/16 have at least one T and at least one R.

questions.stem: Using the same genes (T tall, t short; R red, r white), what phenotypic ratio is expected from the cross TtRr x ttrr?
options: 1 tall red : 1 tall white : 1 short red : 1 short white
questions.explanation: The double heterozygote makes four kinds of gamete (TR, Tr, tR, tr) in equal numbers, and the recessive parent makes only tr.

questions.stem: A man with haemoglobin genotype AS marries a woman with genotype AA. What is the probability that any one of their children will have the genotype AS?
questions.explanation: AS x AA gives 1 AA : 1 AS. None of the children can be SS.

questions.stem: Albinism is caused by a recessive allele. Two parents with normal skin pigment have an albino child. What is the probability that their next child will have normal pigmentation?
questions.explanation: Both parents must be carriers (Aa). Aa x Aa gives 3/4 normal (AA or Aa) and 1/4 albino (aa).

questions.stem: A woman of blood group B has a child of blood group O. What must the woman's genotype be?
questions.explanation: The child (I^O I^O) received an I^O allele from each parent, so the mother must carry I^O as well as I^B.

questions.stem: A cross between two pea plants gave 302 tall and 98 short offspring. What were the most likely genotypes of the parents? (T = tall, t = short)
questions.explanation: 302 : 98 is very close to 3 : 1, the ratio expected from crossing two heterozygotes.

questions.stem: A cell of an organism has a diploid number (2n) of 8 chromosomes. How many chromosomes will each of its gametes contain?
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number, so the gametes are haploid (n = 4).

questions.stem: A Rhesus-negative mother who is carrying her second Rhesus-positive baby may lose the baby because
options: antibodies she made against the Rhesus factor during her first pregnancy can cross the placenta and destroy the baby's red cells
the baby's antibodies attack the mother
questions.explanation: Sensitisation usually happens at the first birth, so later Rhesus-positive babies are at risk. An injection of anti-D after the first birth prevents it.

questions.stem: Three drops were placed on a starch-agar plate: fresh saliva, boiled saliva, and saliva mixed with dilute hydrochloric acid. After an hour at 37 °C, the plate was flooded with iodine solution. A clear zone (no blue-black colour) would be expected around
questions.explanation: Boiling denatures amylase, and strong acid inhibits it, so only fresh saliva digests the starch.

questions.stem: A person whose gall bladder has been removed is often advised to eat less
questions.explanation: Without a store of bile to release after meals, large amounts of fat are not emulsified well.

questions.stem: The rate of photosynthesis of a plant rises as light intensity increases, and then levels off even though the light gets brighter. The levelling off is because
options: the plant has run out of chlorophyll
light always inhibits photosynthesis at high intensity
another factor, such as carbon(IV) oxide concentration or temperature, has become limiting
questions.explanation: By the principle of limiting factors, the rate is controlled by whichever factor is in shortest supply.

questions.stem: A water plant gives off 30 bubbles of gas per minute when a lamp is 10 cm away. The lamp is moved to 20 cm away. If light intensity follows the inverse square law, the light intensity falls to
questions.explanation: Intensity is proportional to 1/d^2. Doubling the distance gives (1/2)^2 = 1/4 of the intensity, so fewer bubbles are released.

questions.stem: Herbivores usually have a much longer alimentary canal (relative to body size) than carnivores because
options: plant food, which is rich in cellulose, is harder to digest and needs more time
carnivores do not digest their food
questions.explanation: A long gut, often with chambers holding microbes, gives more time and space to break down plant material.

questions.stem: Compared with blood in the renal artery, blood in the renal vein contains much less
questions.explanation: The kidneys remove urea from the blood. The kidney cells respire, so the CO2 level actually rises.

questions.stem: Shortly after a meal rich in carbohydrates and proteins, which blood vessel will contain the highest concentration of glucose and amino acids?
questions.explanation: This vein carries blood straight from the absorbing villi to the liver, before the liver adjusts the glucose level.

questions.stem: A person's heart pumps 70 cm^3 of blood with each beat (stroke volume) and beats 72 times per minute. What is the cardiac output?
questions.explanation: Cardiac output = stroke volume x heart rate = 70 x 72 = 5040 cm^3 per minute (about 5 litres).

questions.stem: In a potometer, the air bubble moved 30 mm along a capillary tube with a cross-sectional area of 1 mm^2 in 5 minutes. What was the rate of water uptake?
questions.explanation: Volume = 30 mm x 1 mm^2 = 30 mm^3, taken up in 5 minutes, which gives 6 mm^3 per minute.

questions.stem: Two similar leafy shoots were set up: one had petroleum jelly smeared on the lower surfaces of its leaves, and the other on the upper surfaces. The first shoot lost far less water. This shows that
options: most of the stomata are on the lower surface of the leaves
most of the stomata are on the upper surface
water is lost only through the cuticle
questions.explanation: Blocking the lower surface blocked most of the stomata, through which most transpiration happens.

questions.stem: People who move to live at high altitude, such as on the Mambilla Plateau, gradually produce more red blood cells. This is because
options: the air there contains more carbon(II) oxide
the air there has a lower partial pressure of oxygen
questions.explanation: More red cells (and haemoglobin) make up for the lower oxygen available in each breath.

questions.stem: In a respirometer, germinating seeds are placed in a sealed tube with potassium hydroxide solution, and a coloured drop in the attached capillary moves towards the seeds. This is because
options: the seeds absorb oxygen, and the carbon(IV) oxide they release is absorbed by the KOH, so the volume of gas falls
questions.explanation: The distance the drop moves measures how fast the seeds take up oxygen.

questions.stem: For the complete oxidation of glucose, C6H12O6 + 6O2 -> 6CO2 + 6H2O. What is the respiratory quotient (RQ = volume of CO2 produced / volume of O2 used)?
questions.explanation: Six moles of CO2 are produced for every six moles of O2 used, so RQ = 6/6 = 1.0.

questions.stem: The equation for the complete oxidation of a fat is 2C51H98O6 + 145O2 -> 102CO2 + 98H2O. What is its respiratory quotient?
questions.explanation: RQ = 102/145 = 0.70. Fats contain little oxygen, so they need more O2 per CO2 produced.

questions.stem: Carbon(II) oxide poisoning reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood because carbon(II) oxide
options: destroys the red blood cells immediately
combines with haemoglobin far more firmly than oxygen does
dissolves in plasma and forms an acid
questions.explanation: Carboxyhaemoglobin is very stable, so haemoglobin that has picked up CO is no longer available to carry oxygen.

questions.stem: The concentrations (g per 100 cm^3) of two substances in a healthy kidney are: glucose - plasma 0.10, glomerular filtrate 0.10, urine 0.00; urea - plasma 0.03, filtrate 0.03, urine 2.00. Which conclusion is correct?
options: Glucose is not filtered at the glomerulus
Glucose is filtered and then completely reabsorbed, while urea becomes concentrated in the urine
Neither substance passes into the filtrate
questions.explanation: Equal concentrations in plasma and filtrate show both are filtered. No glucose reaches the urine, while urea becomes about 67 times more concentrated as water is reabsorbed.

questions.stem: In a healthy kidney, the urea concentration is 0.03 g per 100 cm^3 in the glomerular filtrate and 2.0 g per 100 cm^3 in the urine. About how many times more concentrated is urea in the urine than in the filtrate?
questions.explanation: 2.0/0.03 = 66.7, so urea is about 67 times more concentrated. This shows that most of the water is reabsorbed.

questions.stem: Desert mammals such as the camel and desert rat have kidneys with very long loops of Henle. This adaptation
options: allows more water to be reabsorbed, so very concentrated urine is produced
questions.explanation: Long loops build up a high salt concentration in the medulla, which draws water out of the collecting ducts.

questions.stem: On a very hot day, a person produces less urine than usual because
options: more water is lost in sweat, so more ADH is released and more water is reabsorbed in the kidneys
the kidneys stop working in the heat
more glucose appears in the urine
questions.explanation: This helps to keep the water content of the blood constant.

questions.stem: After a head injury, a patient walks unsteadily and cannot coordinate fine movements, but his memory and speech are normal. The part of the brain most likely damaged is the
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates balance and smooth, precise movement.

questions.stem: If the motor neurone in a reflex arc serving the hand is damaged, a person who touches a hot object will
options: feel the pain but be unable to withdraw the hand by reflex
neither feel the pain nor withdraw the hand
withdraw the hand but feel no pain
withdraw the hand faster than usual
questions.explanation: Sensory impulses still reach the spinal cord and brain, but impulses cannot reach the muscles (the effectors).

questions.stem: A diabetic patient who injects too much insulin may become faint and confused because
options: the blood glucose level rises too high
the blood glucose level falls too low to supply the brain
questions.explanation: Excess insulin moves glucose out of the blood into cells and stores, so the brain is short of fuel (hypoglycaemia).

questions.stem: If the tips of oat coleoptiles are cut off and the coleoptiles are lit from one side, they do not bend towards the light. This shows that
options: the base of the coleoptile detects light
the tip produces the substance (auxin) that causes bending
questions.explanation: Putting the tip back on, or placing a block of agar that has absorbed auxin from tips, restores the response.

questions.stem: When the biceps contracts to raise the forearm, the elbow joint acts as the
questions.explanation: The muscle supplies the effort, the hand holds the load, and the elbow is the pivot.

questions.stem: The bones of elderly people break more easily than those of young people mainly because
options: bones grow faster in old age
the bones lose minerals such as calcium and become more brittle
questions.explanation: Loss of bone mineral (osteoporosis) makes bones weaker.

questions.stem: The anthers are removed from a flower bud, and the flower is then covered with a paper bag. No fruit develops. The most likely reason is that
questions.explanation: Without pollen from its own anthers or from other flowers, the ovules were not fertilised.

questions.stem: In maize, the diploid chromosome number (2n) is 20. How many chromosomes are found in each cell of the endosperm?
questions.explanation: The endosperm is triploid (3n), formed when a male nucleus (n) fuses with two polar nuclei (n + n). 3 x 10 = 30.

questions.stem: A flowering plant has a diploid number of 24. How many chromosomes does the pollen tube nucleus contain?
questions.explanation: Pollen grains are formed by meiosis, so all their nuclei are haploid (n = 12).

questions.stem: The combined contraceptive pill, which contains oestrogen and progesterone, prevents pregnancy mainly by
options: preventing menstruation from ever occurring again
suppressing FSH and LH so that ovulation does not occur
questions.explanation: The hormones act on the pituitary gland, as they would naturally during pregnancy.

questions.stem: In a vasectomy,
options: the sperm ducts are cut and tied, so the semen contains no sperm
questions.explanation: It is a permanent method of male contraception that does not affect hormone production.

questions.stem: Moist seeds kept in a refrigerator at about 2 °C do not germinate, mainly because
options: there is no oxygen in a refrigerator
the low temperature slows down the enzyme activity that germination needs
there is no light in a refrigerator
questions.explanation: Enzymes that mobilise food reserves work very slowly at low temperatures.

questions.stem: A graph of the dry mass of a seedling against time falls at first, reaches a minimum and then rises. At the point where dry mass is lowest,
options: the rate of photosynthesis has just become equal to the rate of respiration
the seed has not yet absorbed water
questions.explanation: After this point photosynthesis is faster than respiration, so dry mass increases.

questions.stem: The capture-recapture method of estimating population size assumes that
options: no animals are born or die between samples, and all animals are caught
only marked animals are caught the second time
marked animals mix freely with the rest of the population, and the marks do not affect their survival
questions.explanation: If the marks made animals easier for predators to see, for example, the estimate would be wrong.

questions.stem: A population of 500 grasscutters increases by 10% each year. What will the population be after two years?
questions.explanation: After year 1: 500 x 1.1 = 550. After year 2: 550 x 1.1 = 605. The answer 600 wrongly adds 10% of the original population twice.

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: A persistent insecticide such as DDT enters a lake. The highest concentration of DDT will be found in the tissues of
options: the fish-eating birds at the top of the food chain
questions.explanation: DDT is not broken down or excreted, so it builds up at each trophic level (biological magnification).

questions.topic: Symbiotic interactions of plants and animals
questions.stem: In a food chain, the primary consumers take in 2000 kJ of energy and the secondary consumers take in 180 kJ. What is the efficiency of energy transfer between these two trophic levels?
A 50 g sample of fresh soil weighed 42 g after drying in an oven at 100 °C until its mass stopped changing. What was the percentage of water in the fresh soil?
questions.explanation: Water lost = 50 - 42 = 8 g, and (8/50) x 100 = 16%. 19% wrongly divides by the dry mass.

questions.stem: 40 g of oven-dried soil was heated strongly in a crucible, and its mass fell to 36 g. What was the percentage of humus (organic matter) in the dry soil?
questions.explanation: The organic matter burnt off: (40 - 36)/40 x 100 = 10%.

questions.stem: A farmer finds that his soil has a pH of 4.5, which is too acidic for his crops. He can improve it by adding
questions.explanation: Lime (calcium hydroxide or calcium carbonate) neutralises soil acidity.

questions.stem: Antibiotics such as penicillin are not used to cure AIDS because
options: AIDS is caused by a fungus
antibiotics destroy all white blood cells
antibiotics act against bacteria, but AIDS is caused by a virus
questions.explanation: Viruses have none of the bacterial structures that antibiotics attack. Antiretroviral drugs are used instead.

questions.stem: A river just downstream of a sewage outlet has a very high biochemical oxygen demand (BOD). This indicates that the water
options: is very clean and well oxygenated
contains a lot of decomposing organic matter and has little dissolved oxygen left for animals

questions.stem: The sickle-cell allele is more common in parts of Africa where malaria is widespread than in places without malaria. This is best explained by

people acquiring the allele from mosquitoes
the allele being caused by malaria
natural selection, since carriers (AS) are more likely to survive malaria and pass on the allele
questions.explanation: This is an example of how natural selection keeps a harmful allele in a population because it is useful in one form (the heterozygote).
